analysis.title: SoFi Technologies Inc. (SOFI): 3Q26 Key Takeaways: Shares outperform on stronger growth outlook and limited headwinds from higher rates
key_insights: Shares outperformed after 3Q26, which GS attributes to 2027 guidance roughly 10% ahead of consensus and negative positioning going into the print.

Investors had focused on downside risk to capital and earnings from higher interest rates. The company countered with its interest rate hedging program and its ability to drive growth in a higher rate environment.
Origination momentum was the biggest positive of the quarter, with originations 17% above consensus. Continued personal loan origination momentum could put an upward bias on earnings.
Capital is still the biggest question mark. Capital ratios have fallen about 200bps per quarter for the last 3 quarters.

Management says it has no plans to raise capital. GS notes the quarter's annualized risk-weighted asset (RWA) growth exceeds the balance sheet growth capacity management cited on the call, which points to either slower balance sheet growth or incremental capital needs over the next year.

The company has accelerated growth through more capital-intensive lending over the last year. GS is watching for growth to remix toward lower-yielding loan sales and for origination growth to slow, which could be a revenue headwind over the next year.
GS sees a more balanced risk/reward: strong business momentum offset by a more challenging macro environment, particularly on rates.
3Q26 adjusted revenue was $1,371mn, roughly 8% ahead of consensus. Net interest income was $929.5mn, 9% ahead. Non-interest income was $456mn, 8% ahead.
3Q26 adjusted EBITDA was $470mn, 6% ahead of the Street. Net income was $241mn and EPS was $0.18, slightly ahead of consensus.

FY26 guidance raised: adjusted net revenue ~$5.04bn (from ~$4.75-4.85bn), about 40% growth (from ~34%), adjusted EBITDA ~$1.66bn (from ~$1.6bn), adjusted net income ~$840mn (from $825mn), adjusted diluted EPS ~$0.61 (from ~$0.60).
4Q26 guidance: adjusted net revenue ~$1.375bn, made up of ~$785mn lending, ~$550mn financial services, ~$90mn technology platform, with corporate revenue in line with 3Q.

Initial 2027 guidance: adjusted net revenue ~$6.4bn, adjusted EBITDA ~$2.24bn, adjusted net income ~$1.28bn, adjusted diluted EPS ~$0.90. It targets 30% incremental net income margins and assumes 2 rate hikes and a 24% effective tax rate.
GS raised its 12-month price target to $18 from $15, based on 19x P/E on Q5-Q8 estimates (multiple unchanged). Rating is Neutral, with 9.8% upside from $16.40.
GS EPS estimates for 2026/2027/2028 rose to $0.62/0.81/0.96 from $0.57/0.74/0.84. Revenue estimates rose to $5,145mn/$6,444mn/$7,659.5mn from $4,969.4mn/$5,858.1mn/$6,705.0mn.

market_movers.rationale: Target raised to $18 from $15 on 19x P/E on Q5-Q8 estimates after stronger originations and 2027 guidance about 10% above consensus. Capital ratios falling about 200bps per quarter keep GS at Neutral.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Management's 2027 outlook assumes two rate hikes. Investors had worried about higher rates as a risk to SoFi's capital and earnings, and management pointed to its hedging program as an offset.

Changes in fair value accounting assumptions.

tension_points.bull_case: Originations ran 17% above consensus, 2027 guidance came in about 10% ahead of consensus, and hedging results improved, which GS says removed some downside risk from higher rates.
tension_points.bear_case: Capital ratios have fallen about 200bps per quarter for 3 quarters and RWA growth exceeds the balance sheet growth capacity management cited, implying slower growth or capital needs. Growth could also remix toward lower-yielding loan sales.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Origination growth slowing or the mix shifting toward lower-yielding loan sales would turn the revenue outlook into a headwind over the next year.

theme_stances.key_argument: Strong origination momentum and a better hedging result are offset by falling capital ratios and a tougher rate backdrop, so risk/reward is balanced.
theme_stances.evidence: We see a more balanced risk / reward given the strong momentum
